recentItems.title: Why Egypt sees China as a credible partner, and why it matters
recentItems.description:
For 70 years, China and Egypt have built a remarkable partnership rooted in two ancient civilizations, and their economic ties have grown some 1,700-fold. As momentum continues to build, what opportunities lie ahead? And what could this partnership mean for the wider Arab world, the Middle East and Africa? Don't miss out!

Guest:
Ezzat Saad
Director General, Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs

recentItems.title: The home stretch: Beijing's robot games test physical AI for everyday life
recentItems.description:
Boxing bots, running robots and dexterity duels – Beijing's robot games are putting physical AI to the test. More than 2,000 robots are competing across events that help developers spot weaknesses and sharpen real-world skills, while investors watch closely for the next turning point. Some analysts predict these machines could be in our homes as soon as next year. CGTN’s Chen Jiaqi and Yang Chengxi take you there.

recentItems.title: Pushing through the darkness: The story of Joomart Kokumov
recentItems.description:
Bishkek resident Joomart Kokumov suffered from multiple eye conditions that made it difficult for him to travel by bus on his own, as he could barely see the numbers on the buses. Through the China-Kyrgyzstan "Express Health-Bright Journey" program, Joomart received free eye surgery that significantly improved his vision.

Today, he is able to play goalball, a sport designed for people with visual impairments. And he has a dream: to one day represent Kyrgyzstan on the world stage.

recentItems.title: MAZU: China-Pakistan cooperation to see the storm before it hits
recentItems.description:
A butterfly flapping its wings in Brazil could, in theory, set off a tornado in Texas.

The idea, often used to illustrate the "butterfly effect," captures the complexity of Earth's atmosphere: a tiny disturbance can trigger a chain of changes that eventually develops into a powerful storm. 

For meteorologists, the challenge is to detect those changes as early as possible.

In Pakistan, where extreme weather events are becoming increasingly frequent, a China-developed artificial intelligence platform called MAZU is helping meteorologists strengthen weather forecasting and early warning capabilities, turning vast amounts of atmospheric data into information that can give people more time to prepare.

recentItems.title: Uzbekistan Powers Up with Sunshine
recentItems.description:
Closer cooperation among the Shanghai Cooperation Organization member states in green energy development is encouraging Uzbekistan to turn its abundant sunlight into clean electricity. The country has launched a series of large-scale green energy initiatives, with phase one of a solar project in Namangan already connected to the grid, powering greener development and helping "charge" the future.
